maria: FYI incoming escalation — ACME says their consumer app started getting parser errors when using structured_output/json mode. They receive 200 OK but parser throws JSONDecodeError. They pasted the body: ```{
  "user": "alice",
  "items": [ {"id": 1,}, ]
}``` Billing spiked from client retries. Need quick triage and a recommended pattern for repair/retry (re-ask, self-heal, regex cleanup, backoff).

sam: Thanks, can you add repro steps + raw request (curl) and model + params? Also need correlation_id from their logs.

maria: Pasted curl and headers they used: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"gpt-xl-1","prompt":"extract items as json","structured_output": true, "temperature":0.7, "max_tokens":300}'```

ana: Quick notes from infra: streaming=true can sometimes produce incomplete chunks for naive parsers. First triage checklist: 1) confirm streaming off for strict JSON, 2) set temperature=0 and max_tokens cap, 3) request model name and runtime (dedicated/hosted) + region, 4) capture correlation_id.

sam: For short-term mitigations we usually advise 1) Re-ask pattern: if parse fails, call model again with an explicit instruction to return only valid JSON and include the original malformed response as context. Example re-ask prompt: ```You are a JSON-only assistant. The text below may be malformed JSON. Return exactly one JSON object that strictly follows this schema: {"items": [ {"id": integer, "qty": integer } ] }. If you cannot, return {"__error": "cannot_repair"}. Do not add commentary. Malformed input:
<<<{malformed}>>>``` 2) Self-heal prompt: send to a repair model with temperature=0 and short max_tokens.

lee: Also put a cheap server-side sanitizer before downstream parsing: try quick regex fixes (trailing commas, unquoted keys, stray comments) then attempt json.loads. If still fails, increment backoff and re-ask model for repair.

ana: Sharing common regex heuristics we use (examples): ```# remove JS-style comments: re.sub(r'//.*?$|/\*.*?\*/', '', s, flags=re.M|re.S) # remove trailing commas before ] or }: re.sub(r',(?=\s*[\]}])', '', s) # quote unquoted keys: re.sub(r'(?<=\{|,)(\s*)([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*:', r'"\2":', s)``` Note: heuristics are brittle but often fix simple drift. Always validate after.

maria: Can you also give a tiny python repair snippet to include in support docs?

sam: Sure — share this in the thread as a starting point: ```python
import json, re

def quick_fix_and_parse(s):
    try:
        return json.loads(s)
    except Exception:
        # strip comments
        s2 = re.sub(r'//.*?$|/\*.*?\*/', '', s, flags=re.M|re.S)
        # remove trailing commas
        s2 = re.sub(r',(?=\s*[\]}])', '', s2)
        # quote simple unquoted keys
        s2 = re.sub(r'(?<=\{|,)(\s*)([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*:', r'"\2":', s2)
        try:
            return json.loads(s2)
        except Exception:
            return None  # escalate to repair model
```

ana: Retry/backoff pattern we recommend to customers to avoid billing storms: immediate attempt with in-process repair -> if fail, wait 250ms and re-ask repair model (temp=0) -> if fail, wait 500ms and re-ask -> wait 1s -> final 2s, max 4 attempts. If still broken, return a structured error to client with correlation_id so they can show user-friendly fallback.

lee: Add server-side metric: malformed_json_count per model + per-route so product can alert on schema drift. Also add a small feature flag to auto-repair on the backend for high-volume customers to avoid client retries (that caused the billing break here).

support-bot: Recommended ticket template appended: tags=[escalation,json-repair,high-billing], priority=urgent. Please include: correlation_id, model, runtime, prompt, structured_output flag, temperature, streaming flag, sample malformed response, and whether client already retried.

maria: Great — I'll send mitigation steps to customer: 1) turn off streaming for strict JSON, 2) apply quick-fix regex before client retry, 3) implement re-ask to repair using our repair prompt (temp=0), 4) implement exponential backoff and cap retries, 5) file ticket with correlation_id if the repair fails.

sam: @ana can you create a short KB article from this thread (include regex + python snip + re-ask templates)? I'll fold it into the support playbook and notify CS to refund any overage related to retry storms.

ana: On it. I'll also add an example of a safe response_format schema we can expose via the API to reduce drift.

maria: Thanks everyone. Closing loop: customer currently paused retries; will let us know after we push KB. :thumbsup:
